ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the InP backlog is concentrated in 800G/1.6T AI data-center customers rather than telecom or inventory prebuild; also whether export-permit timing and Tongmei capacity expansion remain on track.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need company-level proof that InP demand is tied to AI datacom customers and not merely telecom recovery, channel inventory, or non-AI photonics demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AXTI is the cleanest underfollowed chokepoint candidate in this chunk: it is upstream of AI optical modules, exposed to InP substrate demand, small-cap, and not widely framed as an AI data-center bandwidth name. The thesis is strong if 800G/1.6T AI datacom ramps create tightness in qualified InP substrates for EML lasers and photonic components.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It screens as a compound-semiconductor substrate and materials company rather than as an AI optical interconnect enabler. Its AI linkage is one layer upstream from transceiver/module demand and can be obscured by telecom, industrial, export-permit, and inventory-cycle noise.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the large InP laser orders are concentrated in a few customers, whether deliveries convert to revenue in 2026-2027, and whether follow-on orders continue into 2027.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need customer/order evidence showing that InP laser equipment demand is tied to AI datacom expansion rather than a one-time customer build, China localization, telecom recovery, or non-AI compound-semiconductor demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: VECO is a second-order capex read-through on InP laser and optical-component manufacturing expansion. It scores highly because it may reveal bottleneck pressure through tool orders before downstream optical revenue fully appears.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is commonly categorized as general semiconductor and compound-semiconductor equipment rather than as a specific AI optical interconnect capacity beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether 448G driver wins convert into production sockets at major transceiver makers and whether gross margin improves as 1.6T/3.2T ramps.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need evidence that design wins are moving from qualification to volume production at AI-oriented transceiver customers, with enough margin contribution to matter at company scale.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: MTSI is a component-level AI optical interconnect candidate through high-speed optical drivers and photonic/RF components for 1.6T and potentially 3.2T links. It is less obscure than AXTI or VECO, but its exposure is still hidden inside RF/analog and photonics classifications.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is often viewed as an RF, microwave, and analog semiconductor company rather than as a platform-agnostic supplier to AI data-center optical links.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether architecture advantages are translating into meaningful production volume and not just design-win rhetoric.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need company-level evidence that AI server or AI accelerator rack customers are converting Vicor modules into material revenue, backlog, gross-margin mix, or named/traceable production programs.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: Vicor sits close to the AI infrastructure chokepoint where rack power density, conversion efficiency, thermals, and proximity-to-load power delivery become deployment constraints. The Serenity logic is strongest when a company has a narrow enabling function that could become harder to substitute as rack power rises. Vicor has a direct enough mapping to AI rack power to justify first-pass priority, but the score is capped because the key claim still requires production-volume evidence rather than design-win language.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is often treated as a niche power-architecture company rather than a direct AI infrastructure beneficiary. That creates a potentially underpriced research angle if AI rack architectures require the kind of high-density modular conversion where Vicor has differentiated exposure.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether customer sampling becomes high-volume production, whether announced partnerships produce binding orders, and whether the company can manufacture at yield and cost targets.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need binding customer orders, volume-production ramps, named transceiver/module ecosystem validation, manufacturing yield evidence, and proof that demand is tied to AI datacenter optics rather than non-AI optical markets.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: POET has high Serenity discovery value because it is one or two steps away from the obvious AI accelerator trade and maps to optical-engine integration, optical interposer, and photonics packaging nodes that could matter as AI clusters move toward 800G, 1.6T, and later 3.2T connectivity. It ranks near the top because the hidden signal is highly testable and the upside to proof would be meaningful, but it remains speculative because current evidence quality is not yet sufficient.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a small-cap photonics platform company that may not screen as an obvious AI semiconductor or data-center infrastructure name. Its relevance is hidden inside optical-engine qualification, manufacturing yield, and packaging economics rather than headline GPU demand.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether growth is tied specifically to 800G/1.6T AI datacom programs and whether capacity additions are customer-backed rather than cyclical telecom recovery.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need AI-specific revenue, capacity, or customer-backed expansion evidence rather than broad optical or telecom-cycle recovery commentary.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: FN offers exposure to precision optical manufacturing, alignment, packaging, and testing capacity required for AI datacom ramps. It ranks below AXTI, VECO, and MTSI because the bottleneck is less structurally scarce and customer confidentiality makes evidence harder to isolate.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is usually screened as contract manufacturing or precision manufacturing, not as a narrow AI networking capacity bottleneck.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether 1.6T production is constrained by lasers, InP substrates, DSP availability, or customer deployment timing.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need detailed production-ramp and constraint evidence that separates customer demand from component availability and internal execution risk.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: AAOI is useful as a downstream demand anchor for validating whether 800G/1.6T AI optical orders are real and whether ramps are constrained by lasers, substrates, DSPs, or customer deployment timing. It is not the best underfollowed discovery, but it is highly falsifiable.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed in this framework; included as a reference name because module-level order timing can validate or falsify the upstream InP substrate and laser-equipment thesis.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether the 1.6T architecture mix shifts toward silicon photonics, EML, or external-light-source designs, and how that affects upstream InP substrate intensity.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need architecture-level disclosure or customer commentary showing whether the next optical generation increases or reduces merchant InP substrate demand.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: LITE is a visible reference anchor for lasers, EMLs, and optical components used in high-speed data-center connectivity. It helps test which optical architecture wins and how much InP intensity remains in the 1.6T transition.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not meaningfully underfollowed; it is included as a downstream technology and component reference rather than as the primary alpha-hunt target.

ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included as a mapping anchor because it spans lasers, optical components, transceivers, and internal substrate or materials capabilities.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AI-driven node shrink, advanced packaging, and HBM-related process complexity are adding incremental process-control intensity beyond normal semiconductor cycle recovery.
ranked_candidates.main_evidence_gap: Need incremental AI-specific process-control intensity evidence rather than broad wafer-fab equipment cycle exposure.
ranked_candidates.why_prioritized: KLA is a high-quality reference node for process control, inspection, and metrology linked to advanced semiconductor manufacturing. However, it is not an underfollowed AI discovery in this chunk and is likely already recognized as a critical semicap supplier.
ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as a reference process-control chokepoint for AI-driven semiconductor complexity.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: How much of current growth is tied to AI-related fab and rack demand versus general semiconductor cycle recovery.

ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is usually categorized as industrial or precision power equipment rather than as an AI infrastructure and AI-fab supply-chain beneficiary.

ranked_candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether AI-related semiconductor and infrastructure demand is visible in sales mix, margins, or backlog commentary.

ranked_candidates.why_underfollowed: It is rarely discussed in AI conversations and is hidden inside broad advanced-materials screens rather than AI optical, AI semicap, or AI infrastructure screens.

The demand durability score is high because AI campuses need reliable power, and gas infrastructure can become an enabling layer when grid interconnection and utility capacity are constrained. However, the rank is reduced because AI exposure is diluted inside a large diversified energy-infrastructure business and requires project-level evidence.

The company has possible exposure to high-efficiency power conversion and electrification layers, but the AI-specific evidence path is weaker than for Vicor or POET. Its rank is held back because financing, utilization, pricing, margins, and execution risk can overwhelm any AI-linked demand signal.
